thread:
alex: Heads-up — the kernel-selection perf numbers from yesterday's replay vs synthetic run are diverging again. Replay shows 12% lower p95 but synthetic is flat. Anyone seen this pattern before?
mina: Yep. Often means the client harness is changing connection/chunking behavior compared to real traffic. Did we compare connection counts + keepalive settings?
dave: +1. Also watch KV cache warmup. Replays that restore KV state produce much better batching efficiency.
alex: We pinned the model and kernels exactly, same hardware. Harnesses used: h2load for gRPC replay and a custom rest-loop for synthetic. Both ran 200 concurrent sessions.
sara: Are you using short-lived HTTP connections for the synthetic harness? If so TLS + handshake + Nagle can inflate latency and reduce effective concurrency.
alex: Synthetic was naive: new HTTP/1.1 connection per request, no keepalive. Oof. That explains a lot.
mina: There you go. Two separate artifacts: 1) connection churn (TLS handshake + CPU) 2) Nagle delaying tiny writes (aggregated into syscalls differently). gRPC (HTTP/2) multiplexing will hide some of that.
dave: Also check client-side connection pool saturation. Our runtime's batching heuristic triggers when N inflight tokens per worker exceed threshold. If client creates bursts across many short conns, you never build dense batches.
mina: For apples-to-apples, ensure both harnesses: 1) use same keepalive and pool sizes, 2) same request pacing (poisson vs burst), 3) same TLS settings (ECDHE curves, session resumption enabled).
perf-bot: perf: note added — compare: synthetic:no-keepalive vs synthetic:keepalive-60s; baseline replay attached.
sara: Small config snippet that helped us — for curl-based rest harness set `--keepalive-time 60` (or use Python requests Session) and tweak `TCP_NODELAY` off vs on to reproduce Nagle. Example pseudo-config: ```
client:
  connections: 50
  keepalive_seconds: 60
  reuse_sessions: true
  tcp_nodelay: true
  request_rate: 120rps
```
dave: On gRPC side, ensure channel is reused across threads. If you create a new Channel per request you lose multiplexing. In Go: reuse `grpc.Dial` and share the client stub.
mina: Another gotcha: TLS session resumption. Our replay env had memcached-backed session store on the LB, synthetic didn't. That single difference cut handshake CPU dramatically.
alex: Good checklist. I also noticed kernel-selection improvements only show up when batches hit >8 tokens avg. If your client pattern prevents large batches (due to churn), the kernel never gets exercised.
sara: For profiling: capture both kernel selection traces and per-request TCP metrics. We do `bcc` on the runtime and `ss` on the client to correlate handshake rates.
dave: Quick repro plan: 1) Enable keepalive and session reuse on synthetic. 2) Run warmup phase to populate KV cache and kernel caches. 3) Run same poisson inter-arrival workload with identical concurrency. 4) Collect kernel-selection logs + e2e p50/p95 + cpu breakdown.
mina: Also add a run with `tcp_nodelay=false` to see Nagle impact on small-response models. Expect higher latency variance but lower syscalls.
alex: I'll patch the harness and run the plan. If results still diverge I'll attach traces. Thanks — saved a day. :thumbsup:
sara: Happy to pair if you want to instrument the client side. I have small scripts to force TLS resumption and pin keepalive sockets.
